title: THE DAY WREN WAS RIGHT
deck: A floating market of twelve hundred households has thirty days to meet a sanitation law it genuinely breaks, and the plan that would save it is wrong in the one way only Wren could see.
shape: A rebuild in six scenes: the clean plan fails on a companion's objection, a hand-kept ledger turns out to be the system itself with three holes, a sealed-prediction sampling beats the loud rival cause, a council decides what each party will and will not give, two excluded households keep their objections, and the water reads the result while the lease and the ledger stay in different hands.

scenes.title: The Clean Plan
paragraphs: *Harbour Office quay, Sorrel Water · Day 3 of 30, 08:10*
The Order was fourteen pages long and gave thirty days, and on the third morning Illuminara laid her answer across the Harbour Office counter on a single sheet.

Twelve hundred boat-households lived on Kettle Market. The Harbourmaster's Sanitation Order No. 14 said that after the fifteenth of November none of them could go on discharging into Sorrel Water, and the August samples had shown the Order was right. Illuminara's sheet showed a licensed pump-out barge, six fixed stops, a sensor in every tank and one monthly bill.

**Cedric Aldana**  
It is the cleanest compliance plan anyone has put in front of me. Every vessel metered, every pump-out logged. I could sign it on a Friday.
Wren Odira came up the quay steps with smoke in her coat and river mud to the knee. She had spent three weeks sleeping on other people's decks. She read the sheet standing, twice, and set it down.

**Wren Odira**  
It will fail.

**Illuminara**  
Tell me where it breaks first.

**Wren Odira**  
Wherever the barge is when the string has moved. Kettle doesn't sit at six stops. It re-rafts on every ebb, and boats slide to be near the boats they owe. Your stop six holds a hundred and forty hulls on Monday and sixty on Thursday. And you meter the tank. Whoever pays by the tank learns to keep it half empty and the hose long.

**Illuminara**  
A meter that pays a family to leave the harbour dirty. I did not model that.

**Wren Odira**  
You modelled a machine. It's a rumour with a rota.
Illuminara did not defend the sheet. *Wren has the shape of it. I do not yet have one fact worth more than her three weeks.*

**Illuminara**  
Then something is already working. In August the water was bad, not lethal, and Kettle has lived on it for thirty years. Who keeps the record of how?

**Wren Odira**  
There's a book.

**Cedric Aldana**  
The Order wants a record for each vessel. A book is not a record.
He had said wants, not requires, and his hand had gone to the folded Order in his breast pocket before he said it. *He is not refusing. He is telling me there is a door and that he may not open it.*

**Illuminara**  
Is there anything the Order wants more than a record for each vessel?

**Cedric Aldana**  
There is something it will accept in its place. It needs three things at once: a lease, clean water at the outfall, and a signer I can inspect without warning. Kettle has never had a signer. If I name an arrangement and it fails, the failure is mine, so I do not name it.

**Illuminara**  
You have just named three things.

**Cedric Aldana**  
I have recited a regulation. That is allowed.

**Illuminara**  
Then I would like to read the book before I tell you what a record is.

scenes.title: The Tie-Book
paragraphs: *Dock-mistress's counter, Kettle Market · Day 4, 06:00*
Odalys Ferreira kept eleven volumes of the tie-book under her counter, in pencil, because ink runs on a wet quay. She laid the current one open and kept one hand flat on it.

**Odalys Ferreira**  
You may read here. You may not copy a page, and if I see you reading a name you weren't asked to, I close it. This book is the only thing on the water that nobody has ever been able to buy.

Illuminara read for six hours. *Selka carried Reed 3, 5, 7. Tues. Pump to Mill 2, from Gwil. Back by dusk. Tied: Aurelian, visitor.* Line by line she let the entries fall into place as a graph: strings of rafted boats, carriers who wheeled the waste to the barge quay on days each string had chosen, pumps that travelled on a promise.
Nobody had written down a rota. The book was the rota, kept in the one language the market trusted.

**Illuminara**  
Eight boats in ten pass their waste to a carrier, the carrier takes it to the licensed quay, and the book shows eleven years of corrections. Thirty-eight strings, and none has ever asked the Harbourmaster for anything.

**Wren Odira**  
I told you.

**Illuminara**  
You did, and you were right about the form. It fails in three places, and I find them by what the book leaves out. First, Reed Row. Tuesdays and Fridays, every week for eleven years. Not one carry on a Sunday.

**Odalys Ferreira**  
Sunday is rest. Reed Row rests hardest of any string.

**Illuminara**  
Look at the pump-loan pages. They list tank sizes, and Reed Row's are the smallest in the harbour. Look at the tie entries. Visitors raft on Reed Row on Fridays and Saturdays, and the Friday carry empties the tanks before they arrive. And here, on the margin of volume six: relief valve, Reed Row, mended. Four times in eleven years, always on a Monday.

**Odalys Ferreira**  
A valve is a valve.

**Illuminara**  
A relief valve lifts when a tank is full and has nowhere to go. A full tank, a guest weekend, no carrier, and the Sunday ebb to carry it away.
Odalys looked at the margin as if someone else had written it. She said nothing, which in her was an answer.

**Illuminara**  
Second. Every pump loan in this volume names Gwil Anand, or Gwil's spare. One pump, one owner, and he is seventy-nine.

**Odalys Ferreira**  
Gwil Anand will outlive the harbour.

**Illuminara**  
Third, and it is the one the Inspector cares about. Nothing here lets the Order learn that any of this happened without opening the book to him.

**Odalys Ferreira**  
That is what the book is for.

**Illuminara**  
I know. I will come back to it. But the first two I only suspect, and half this harbour will say the water is dirty because of the tannery drain upstream.

**Wren Odira**  
They'll say it before you've finished the sentence.

**Illuminara**  
Then we measure before anyone claims anything.

scenes.title: Four Stations
paragraphs: *Sorrel Water, on the ebb · Saturday 22:00 to Monday 06:00*

Pia Zane, who ran the Inspector's small laboratory out of a van, set four sample stations: one above the market, one at the mouth of Reed Row, one mid-market, one below it. Illuminara told her which results would count against Illuminara.

She wrote the predictions on a card, sealed it, and gave it to Aldana before the first bottle was filled. If the Sunday gap was real, Reed Row's mouth would read at least five times its Saturday figure on the Sunday ebb while the station above the market stayed flat. If the tannery was the cause, the upstream station would be high on both nights and Reed Row would barely differ from it. If neither, everything would be flat and she would have been wrong about the book.

The card also said that the fourth station, below the market, was the outfall, and that the standard of two hundred applied there and nowhere else. Reed Row would read high at its own mouth. That was a diagnosis, not a pass.

**Hesper Quill**  
You are sampling Reed Row on our day of rest. You will write our shame in water and hand it to the Inspector.

**Illuminara**  
I am sampling the one place your string cannot answer for. If the number is bad on Sunday, it will be the first fact either of us has that is ours to fix.

**Hesper Quill**  
And if it's bad on Saturday too?

**Illuminara**  
Then I am wrong, and the card says so.
Wren rowed the bottles herself, one leg of the route at a time. The numbers came back on Monday at six, in enterococci per hundred millilitres.

**Pia Zane**  
Saturday ebb. Upstream, ninety. Reed Row, two hundred and ten. Mid-market, a hundred and eighty. Below the market, two hundred and sixty. Sunday ebb. Upstream, a hundred and ten. Reed Row, two thousand three hundred. Mid-market, six-forty. Below, seven hundred.

**Wren Odira**  
Upstream is flat.

**Pia Zane**  
The tannery adds something after rain. It is not this.

**Illuminara**  
The tannery is a fact and it is not this fact. It will still be there when we finish, and I will say so to the council myself, so nobody has to hear it from the other side.
Hesper Quill read the Sunday line twice. She did not apologise and she did not argue. She asked what it would cost her people to stop it.

scenes.title: Three Links
paragraphs: *The council deck, Kettle Market · Day 9, 19:00*
Thirty-eight string-wardens came, and Aldana came with his Order folded in his pocket. Illuminara had drawn only three additions to the system they already ran, and she said so first.

**Illuminara**  
I am not bringing you a new system. You have one. I am bringing three links it is missing, and each of you can refuse yours.

**Hesper Quill**  
Reed Row will carry its own Sunday. We won't do it under anybody's name in a book the Inspector reads.

**Selka Dunmore**  
Tam and I will swap. I take Reed's Sunday and Reed takes my Monday. That's a trade among neighbours. It is not a rota for the Harbour Office.

**Illuminara**  
That is the first link, and it is better than mine. I had a paid Sunday carrier. Yours costs nothing and will outlast any budget.

**Hesper Quill**  
It is not free. Tam works a day he has never worked, and Reed Row pays him for it out of our own purse. We will not ask the council for it.

**Gwil Anand**  
And you want my pump.

**Illuminara**  
I want a second one, floated mid-market and lent only through you. If you fall ill, the loan does not stop. You stay the one people ask.

**Gwil Anand**  
If I'm still the one they ask, I'll lend it.
Then Aldana unfolded the Order.

**Cedric Aldana**  
I must have a record for each vessel. I do not make the clause.

**Illuminara**  
Then read the clause again, Inspector. Section six, paragraph b. An equivalent community arrangement may be certified in place of a vessel record if it is held under a lease, if the water at the outfall meets the standard, and if the body that signs can be inspected without notice. It asks for outcomes. It does not ask for names.

**Illuminara**  
The book is why the water is clean, and the book will not leave Odalys's counter. The council holds a lease. The water is measured at the three stations, once a month, on random days. And the body that signs is this council, whose only signed paper is a count of carries with no boat named, so that you can walk in unannounced and count the tickets.

**Odalys Ferreira**  
You are telling me to hand the Harbourmaster a number and keep the book.

**Illuminara**  
I am telling you the number is what he is allowed to ask for.

**Wren Odira**  
And a lease. Ten years. That is a leash, and a short one. In year ten they let go of it and Kettle is a fine.

**Cedric Aldana**  
Ten is what the paragraph permits.

**Illuminara**  
Ten is what the law gives this month. I would rather ask for ten and keep the market alive than ask for thirty and meet the Harbourmaster in court with money Kettle does not have.

**Wren Odira**  
That is your arithmetic. It is not mine.

Illuminara let it stand. The vote was the council's. Thirty-one strings voted yes and seven voted no, and the minute recorded the seven refusals, to be read out again at every renewal. Neither she nor Wren could take it from the other.

scenes.title: The Two Boats
paragraphs: *The smokehouse Ember, tied at the east edge · Day 14, dusk*

Torvald Beck's smoke-boat had been a ferry hull once, and no holding tank would fit it. Iliana Dross's Aurelian was registered upriver at Cress Market and had been in the tie-book as visitor fourteen times.

**Torvald Beck**  
I have read the plan. It was written for the boats that were already inside the book.

**Iliana Dross**  
My name is in your book fourteen times, and in not one of them as a member. I carry my own waste out of this harbour. I have done it for nine years. I will not be counted by your rota or inspected by your Inspector.

**Illuminara**  
He is right, Iliana. The book holds only those who tie, and I read the market through it. That is a hole in my method, not only in the plan.
She turned to Wren, who had sat on Beck's deck three nights running and eaten his fish.

**Wren Odira**  
I have two requests. That Beck and Dross each sit at the council until the lease is signed. And that the Sunday fund Reed Row opened for Tam also pays for whatever Beck needs, because he will not ask.

**Illuminara**  
Hesper has said yes to that, and I asked her last night. Beck, a sealed float-tank towed astern of Ember, nineteen hundred marks, built by Gwil's apprentice. It is not elegant. It would work.

**Torvald Beck**  
And my name stays out of the Reed Row sheet.

**Illuminara**  
It was never in it.

**Torvald Beck**  
Then the council can vote on the tank.

**Iliana Dross**  
I tie here eleven days a year. I will not be inspected for the other three hundred and fifty-four.

**Illuminara**  
Then I will not ask you to be counted. A free rinse at the barge quay on any day you tie, with no entry in anyone's book. If the water reads clean in spring, you will know whose doing that was, and you can decide again.
Dross did not say yes. She weighed it the way a woman weighs a rope. In the morning the Aurelian had cast off for Cress Market, with a day-pass in her pocket and her reasons unrevised.

scenes.title: What the Water Said
paragraphs: *The quay and Reed Row · Day 27, 17:00*
The trial had run ten days: Reed Row's Sunday carriers, Gwil's second pump on its float, and the Ember's tank, towed astern and humming faintly with a pump of its own.

**Pia Zane**  
Sunday ebb. Upstream, a hundred and five. Reed Row, three hundred and ten. Mid-market, a hundred and seventy. Below the market, one hundred and ninety.

**Cedric Aldana**  
Reed Row from twenty-three hundred to three hundred and ten at its own mouth. Below the market from seven hundred to one-ninety. The outfall is under two hundred.

**Pia Zane**  
The tannery is still adding its share. It is a hundred and five. The standard at the outfall is two hundred.

Aldana read the certificate aloud. It named the Kettle Council as the signing body, ten years as the term, three stations, random sampling and no list of boats. He signed under the line. Hesper Quill signed beneath him. Nobody cheered, because the water was still brown and the standard was still a number on a van.

**Wren Odira**  
I still say ten is a leash.

**Illuminara**  
So do I. What would you change?

**Wren Odira**  
Post the three numbers on the quay every month, where any boat can read them. A lease the whole harbour can read is harder to cancel than one in a drawer.

**Illuminara**  
That is stronger than the clause I wrote. Put it to the council.
Odalys opened the book on the counter. She did not ask permission and she did not offer to show it. She wrote one line, in pencil.
*Sunday, Reed 7. Carried. Tam.*

**Illuminara**  
May I see the page?

**Odalys Ferreira**  
No. It is not your page.

Illuminara smiled, which was not a thing she often did in front of strangers. Out on the water the ebb ran past the market a little clearer than on the day she arrived, and Wren, who had been right on the first morning and would be right about the lease in ten years, stood on the quay and read the numbers aloud to the boats.

critic_line: A floating market survives a deserved sanitation deadline because Illuminara treats Wren's objection as a better model, proves the Sunday leak with a sealed test, and builds an inspectable outcome around the community's own private tie-book without seizing it.

literary_score.method: Independent GPT 7D SA1 and Claude PEC-6 final scores; equal 50/50 model weight.
shared_strengths: Both judges praised the tie-book inference and sealed-prediction sampling as a clear, falsifiable causal route from observation to bounded intervention.
Both judges found that dissent and data ownership survive the success: Wren, Odalys, Hesper, Beck and Dross retain choices Illuminara cannot absorb.
shared_reservations: Both judges noted stylised, expository dialogue and secondary characters whose civic functions are clearer than their private textures.
Both judges found the legal and public-health turnaround somewhat cleaner than the surrounding world, with limited personal pressure on Illuminara.

translation_sl.title: DAN, KO JE IMELA WREN PRAV
translation_sl.deck: Plavajoča tržnica z dvanajststo gospodinjstvi ima trideset dni, da izpolni sanitarni zakon, ki ga resnično krši, načrt, ki bi jo rešil, pa je napačen prav na edini način, ki ga je lahko opazila Wren.
translation_sl.shape: Prenova v šestih prizorih: čist načrt propade zaradi ugovora spremljevalke, ročno vodena knjiga se izkaže za sam sistem s tremi vrzelmi, vzorčenje z zapečateno napovedjo premaga glasni konkurenčni vzrok, svet določi, kaj bo vsaka stran dala in česa ne, dve izključeni gospodinjstvi ohranita svoje ugovore, voda pa prebere izid, medtem ko zakup in knjiga ostaneta v različnih rokah.

scenes.title: Čisti načrt
paragraphs: *Pomol pristaniškega urada, Sorrel Water · 3. dan od 30, 08:10*
Odredba je bila dolga štirinajst strani in je določala trideset dni, tretje jutro pa je Illuminara svoj odgovor razgrnila čez pult pristaniškega urada na enem samem listu.

Na tržnici Kettle je živelo dvanajststo gospodinjstev na barkah. Sanitarna odredba pristaniškega poveljnika št. 14 je določala, da po petnajstem novembru nobeno od njih ne sme več izpuščati odplak v Sorrel Water, avgustovski vzorci pa so pokazali, da ima odredba prav. Illuminarin list je prikazoval licencirano barko za praznjenje, šest stalnih postaj, senzor v vsakem rezervoarju in en mesečni račun.

**Cedric Aldana**  
To je najčistejši načrt za skladnost, kar mi jih je kdo položil pred oči. Vsako plovilo izmerjeno, vsako praznjenje zabeleženo. Podpisal bi ga lahko v petek.
Wren Odira se je povzpela po stopnicah pomola z dimom v plašču in rečnim blatom do kolen. Tri tedne je spala na palubah drugih ljudi. List je dvakrat prebrala stoje in ga odložila.

**Wren Odira**  
Propadel bo.

**Illuminara**  
Povej mi, kje bo najprej počil.

**Wren Odira**  
Povsod, kjer bo barka, ko se bo niz premaknil. Kettle ne miruje pri šestih postajah. Ob vsaki oseki se na novo poveže v splave in barke drsijo bliže barkam, ki jim nekaj dolgujejo. Na tvoji šesti postaji je v ponedeljek sto štirideset trupov, v četrtek pa šestdeset. In meriš rezervoar. Kdor plačuje po rezervoarju, se nauči, kako ga ohraniti napol praznega in cev dolgo.

**Illuminara**  
Merilnik, ki družino nagradi, če pusti pristanišče umazano. Tega nisem vključila v model.

**Wren Odira**  
Modelirala si stroj. To pa je govorica z razporedom.
Illuminara lista ni branila. *Wren razume njegovo obliko. Sama še nimam niti enega dejstva, vrednega več od njenih treh tednov.*

**Illuminara**  
Potem nekaj že deluje. Avgusta je bila voda slaba, ne smrtonosna, Kettle pa na njej živi trideset let. Kdo vodi zapis o tem, kako?

**Wren Odira**  
Obstaja knjiga.

**Cedric Aldana**  
Odredba zahteva zapis za vsako plovilo. Knjiga ni zapis.

Rekel je zahteva, ne pa predpisuje, in roka mu je segla k prepognjeni odredbi v prsnem žepu, še preden je besedo izgovoril. *Ne zavrača. Govori mi, da obstajajo vrata, ki jih sam morda ne sme odpreti.*

**Illuminara**  
Ali odredba hoče kaj še bolj kot zapis za vsako plovilo?

**Cedric Aldana**  
Obstaja nekaj, kar bo sprejela namesto njega. Hkrati potrebuje tri stvari: zakup, čisto vodo pri iztoku in podpisnika, ki ga lahko brez opozorila pregledam. Kettle nikoli ni imel podpisnika. Če določim ureditev in ta propade, je neuspeh moj, zato je ne bom določil.

**Illuminara**  
Pravkar ste določili tri stvari.

**Cedric Aldana**  
Navedel sem predpis. To je dovoljeno.

**Illuminara**  
Potem bi rada prebrala knjigo, preden vam povem, kaj je zapis.

scenes.title: Privezna knjiga
paragraphs: *Pult upravnice pomola, tržnica Kettle · 4. dan, 06:00*
Odalys Ferreira je pod svojim pultom hranila enajst zvezkov privezne knjige, zapisane s svinčnikom, ker črnilo na mokrem pomolu steče. Odprla je tekoči zvezek in na njem držala eno dlan.

**Odalys Ferreira**  
Berete lahko tukaj. Strani ne smete prepisati, in če vas zalotim, da berete ime, za katero vas niso vprašali, knjigo zaprem. To je edina stvar na vodi, ki je še nihče ni mogel kupiti.

Illuminara je brala šest ur. *Selka je peljala Reed 3, 5, 7. Tor. Črpanje pri Mill 2, od Gwila. Nazaj do mraka. Privezani: Aurelian, obiskovalec.* Vrstico za vrstico je pustila, da so se vnosi sestavili v graf: nizi skupaj privezanih bark, prevozniki, ki so odpadke na dneve po izbiri posameznega niza vozili do pomola črpalne barke, ter črpalke, ki so potovale na dano besedo.
Nihče ni zapisal razporeda. Knjiga je bila razpored, voden v edinem jeziku, ki mu je tržnica zaupala.

**Illuminara**  
Osem bark od desetih preda odpadke prevozniku, prevoznik jih pelje do licenciranega pomola, knjiga pa kaže enajst let popravkov. Osemintrideset nizov, nobeden pa pristaniškega poveljnika še nikoli ni prosil za nič.

**Wren Odira**  
Saj sem ti povedala.

**Illuminara**  
Si, in glede oblike si imela prav. Sistem odpove na treh mestih, najdem pa jih po tem, česar knjiga ne vsebuje. Prvo je Reed Row. Ob torkih in petkih, vsak teden enajst let. Niti enega prevoza v nedeljo.

**Odalys Ferreira**  
Nedelja je počitek. Reed Row počiva najbolj od vseh nizov.

**Illuminara**  
Poglejte strani o posojanju črpalk. Na njih so zapisane velikosti rezervoarjev, na Reed Row pa so najmanjši v pristanišču. Poglejte vnose privezov. Obiskovalci se v petek in soboto privežejo k Reed Row, petkov prevoz pa rezervoarje izprazni pred njihovim prihodom. In tukaj, na robu šestega zvezka: razbremenilni ventil, Reed Row, popravljen. Štirikrat v enajstih letih, vedno v ponedeljek.

**Odalys Ferreira**  
Ventil je ventil.

**Illuminara**  
Razbremenilni ventil se odpre, ko je rezervoar poln in vsebina nima kam. Poln rezervoar, obiskovalci čez konec tedna, nobenega prevoznika in nedeljska oseka, ki vse odnese.
Odalys je rob pogledala, kakor da bi ga napisal nekdo drug. Ni rekla ničesar, kar je bilo pri njej odgovor.

**Illuminara**  
Drugo. Vsako posojilo črpalke v tem zvezku navaja Gwila Ananda ali Gwilovo rezervno črpalko. Ena črpalka, en lastnik, on pa ima devetinsedemdeset let.

**Odalys Ferreira**  
Gwil Anand bo preživel pristanišče.

**Illuminara**  
Tretje, in to je tisto, kar zanima inšpektorja. Tukaj nič ne omogoča, da bi odredba izvedela, da se je karkoli od tega zgodilo, ne da bi mu odprli knjigo.

**Odalys Ferreira**  
Temu je knjiga namenjena.

**Illuminara**  
Vem. K temu se bom vrnila. Toda prva dva sta za zdaj le moj sum, polovica pristanišča pa bo rekla, da je voda umazana zaradi usnjarskega odtoka više ob reki.

**Wren Odira**  
To bodo rekli, še preden boš dokončala stavek.

**Illuminara**  
Potem bomo merili, preden bo kdorkoli karkoli zatrjeval.

scenes.title: Štiri postaje
paragraphs: *Sorrel Water med oseko · od sobote, 22:00, do ponedeljka, 06:00*

Pia Zane, ki je iz kombija vodila inšpektorjev majhen laboratorij, je postavila štiri vzorčne postaje: eno nad tržnico, eno pri ustju Reed Row, eno sredi tržnice in eno pod njo. Illuminara ji je povedala, kateri rezultati bi govorili proti Illuminari.

Napovedi je zapisala na kartico, jo zapečatila in pred polnjenjem prve steklenice izročila Aldani. Če je nedeljska vrzel resnična, bo ustje Reed Row ob nedeljski oseki pokazalo vsaj petkrat sobotno vrednost, postaja nad tržnico pa bo ostala nespremenjena. Če je vzrok usnjarna, bo postaja više ob reki obe noči kazala veliko, Reed Row pa se bo od nje komaj razlikoval. Če ni ne eno ne drugo, bo povsod enako in njeno branje knjige bo napačno.

Na kartici je pisalo tudi, da je četrta postaja, pod tržnico, iztok ter da standard dvesto velja tam in nikjer drugje. Reed Row bo pri lastnem ustju pokazal veliko. To bo diagnoza, ne potrdilo skladnosti.

**Hesper Quill**  
Reed Row vzorčite na naš dan počitka. Našo sramoto boste zapisali v vodo in jo izročili inšpektorju.

**Illuminara**  
Vzorčim edino mesto, za katero vaš niz ne more jamčiti. Če bo številka v nedeljo slaba, bo to prvo dejstvo, ki ga imava obe in ga lahko popravimo.

**Hesper Quill**  
Kaj pa, če bo slaba tudi v soboto?

**Illuminara**  
Potem se motim, in tako piše tudi na kartici.
Wren je sama odveslala po steklenice, odsek za odsekom. Rezultati so prispeli v ponedeljek ob šestih, v enterokokih na sto mililitrov.

**Pia Zane**  
Sobotna oseka. Više ob reki devetdeset. Reed Row dvesto deset. Sredi tržnice sto osemdeset. Pod tržnico dvesto šestdeset. Nedeljska oseka. Više ob reki sto deset. Reed Row dva tisoč tristo. Sredi tržnice šeststo štirideset. Spodaj sedemsto.

**Wren Odira**  
Više ob reki je nespremenjeno.

**Pia Zane**  
Usnjarna po dežju nekaj doda. To ni to.

**Illuminara**  
Usnjarna je dejstvo, ni pa to dejstvo. Tam bo še vedno, ko bomo končali, in to bom svetu povedala sama, da tega nikomur ne bo treba slišati z druge strani.
Hesper Quill je nedeljsko vrstico prebrala dvakrat. Ni se opravičila in ni ugovarjala. Vprašala je, koliko bo njene ljudi stalo, da to ustavijo.

scenes.title: Tri povezave
paragraphs: *Paluba sveta, tržnica Kettle · 9. dan, 19:00*
Prišlo je osemintrideset varuhov nizov, Aldana pa je prišel z odredbo, prepognjeno v žepu. Illuminara je sistemu, ki so ga že vodili, dodala le tri stvari in je to povedala najprej.

**Illuminara**  
Ne prinašam vam novega sistema. Enega že imate. Prinašam tri povezave, ki mu manjkajo, vsako od njih pa lahko zavrnete.

**Hesper Quill**  
Reed Row bo sam poskrbel za svojo nedeljo. Tega ne bomo počeli pod imenom kogarkoli v knjigi, ki jo bere inšpektor.

**Selka Dunmore**  
S Tamom bova zamenjala. Jaz prevzamem Reedovo nedeljo, Reed pa moj ponedeljek. To je menjava med sosedi. Ni razpored za pristaniški urad.

**Illuminara**  
To je prva povezava in boljša je od moje. Sama sem predvidela plačanega nedeljskega prevoznika. Vaša ne stane nič in bo preživela vsak proračun.

**Hesper Quill**  
Ni zastonj. Tam dela na dan, ko še nikoli ni delal, Reed Row pa mu za to plača iz lastne blagajne. Sveta ne bomo prosili za denar.

**Gwil Anand**  
In vi hočete mojo črpalko.

**Illuminara**  
Hočem drugo, nameščeno na plovec sredi tržnice in posojeno samo prek vas. Če zbolite, se posojanje ne ustavi. Vi ostanete tisti, ki ga ljudje vprašajo.

**Gwil Anand**  
Če še vedno mene vprašajo, jo bom posojal.
Tedaj je Aldana razgrnil odredbo.

**Cedric Aldana**  
Imeti moram zapis za vsako plovilo. Klavzule ne določam jaz.

**Illuminara**  
Potem klavzulo preberite še enkrat, inšpektor. Šesti člen, odstavek b. Enakovredna skupnostna ureditev se lahko potrdi namesto zapisa o plovilu, če je sklenjena z zakupom, če voda pri iztoku ustreza standardu in če je mogoče telo, ki se podpiše, pregledati brez opozorila. Zahteva izide. Ne zahteva imen.

**Illuminara**  
Knjiga je razlog, da je voda čista, in ne bo zapustila Odalysinega pulta. Svet ima zakup. Voda se enkrat mesečno meri na treh postajah, na naključne dni. Telo, ki se podpiše, pa je ta svet, katerega edini podpisani papir je število prevozov brez imen bark, zato lahko vstopite brez opozorila in preštejete listke.

**Odalys Ferreira**  
Pravite mi, naj pristaniškemu poveljniku dam številko, knjigo pa obdržim.

**Illuminara**  
Pravim vam, da je številka vse, kar sme zahtevati.

**Wren Odira**  
In zakup. Deset let. To je povodec, in še kratek. V desetem letu ga spustijo in Kettle postane globa.

**Cedric Aldana**  
Deset je toliko, kolikor dovoljuje odstavek.

**Illuminara**  
Deset je toliko, kolikor nam ta mesec daje zakon. Raje prosim za deset in ohranim tržnico pri življenju, kakor da prosim za trideset in se s pristaniškim poveljnikom srečam na sodišču z denarjem, ki ga Kettle nima.

**Wren Odira**  
To je tvoja računica. Ni moja.

Illuminara je pustila, da obvelja. Glasovanje je pripadalo svetu. Enaintrideset nizov je glasovalo za, sedem proti, v zapisnik pa so vnesli sedem zavrnitev, ki jih bodo znova prebrali ob vsakem podaljšanju. Ne ona ne Wren je nista mogli odvzeti drugi.

scenes.title: Dve barki
paragraphs: *Dimna barka Ember, privezana na vzhodnem robu · 14. dan, mrak*

Dimna barka Torvalda Becka je bila nekoč trajekt in vanjo ni bilo mogoče namestiti nobenega zadrževalnega rezervoarja. Aurelian Iliane Dross je bil registriran više ob reki, na tržnici Cress, v privezni knjigi pa je bil štirinajstkrat vpisan kot obiskovalec.

**Torvald Beck**  
Prebral sem načrt. Napisan je bil za barke, ki so bile že v knjigi.

**Iliana Dross**  
Moje ime je v vaši knjigi štirinajstkrat in niti enkrat kot članica. Svoje odpadke sama odpeljem iz tega pristanišča. To počnem že devet let. Ne bom se pustila šteti po vašem razporedu ali pregledovati vašemu inšpektorju.

**Illuminara**  
Prav ima, Iliana. V knjigi so samo tisti, ki se privežejo, sama pa sem tržnico brala skoznjo. To je vrzel v moji metodi, ne le v načrtu.
Obrnila se je k Wren, ki je tri noči zapored sedela na Beckovi palubi in jedla njegove ribe.

**Wren Odira**  
Imam dve zahtevi. Da Beck in Dross sedita v svetu, dokler zakup ni podpisan. In da nedeljski sklad, ki ga je Reed Row odprl za Tama, plača tudi vse, kar potrebuje Beck, ker sam ne bo prosil.

**Illuminara**  
Hesper je s tem soglašala in vprašala sem jo sinoči. Beck, zapečaten plavajoči rezervoar, ki bi ga vlekli za Ember, tisoč devetsto mark, izdelal pa bi ga Gwilov vajenec. Ni eleganten. Deloval bi.

**Torvald Beck**  
Moje ime pa ostane zunaj lista Reed Row.

**Illuminara**  
Nikoli ga ni bilo na njem.

**Torvald Beck**  
Potem lahko svet glasuje o rezervoarju.

**Iliana Dross**  
Tukaj se privežem enajst dni na leto. Preostalih tristo štiriinpetdeset dni ne bom dovolila pregledovanja.

**Illuminara**  
Potem vas ne bom prosila, da vas štejejo. Brezplačno izpiranje pri pomolu črpalne barke na katerikoli dan, ko se privežete, brez vnosa v katerokoli knjigo. Če bo voda spomladi čista, boste vedeli, čigavo delo je bilo, in se boste lahko znova odločili.
Dross ni rekla da. Pretehtala je ponudbo tako, kakor ženska pretehta vrv. Zjutraj je Aurelian odplul proti tržnici Cress, z dnevnim dovoljenjem v njenem žepu in njenimi razlogi nespremenjenimi.

scenes.title: Kar je povedala voda
paragraphs: *Pomol in Reed Row · 27. dan, 17:00*
Poskus je trajal deset dni: nedeljski prevozniki Reed Row, Gwilova druga črpalka na plovcu in Emberjev rezervoar, ki ga je vlekla za seboj in je tiho brnel z lastno črpalko.

**Pia Zane**  
Nedeljska oseka. Više ob reki sto pet. Reed Row tristo deset. Sredi tržnice sto sedemdeset. Pod tržnico sto devetdeset.

**Cedric Aldana**  
Reed Row z dva tisoč tristo na tristo deset pri lastnem ustju. Pod tržnico s sedemsto na sto devetdeset. Iztok je pod dvesto.

**Pia Zane**  
Usnjarna še vedno prispeva svoj delež. Ta je sto pet. Standard pri iztoku je dvesto.

Aldana je potrdilo prebral na glas. Kot podpisno telo je imenovalo svet Kettle, kot obdobje deset let, tri postaje, naključno vzorčenje in nobenega seznama bark. Pod vrstico se je podpisal. Pod njim se je podpisala Hesper Quill. Nihče ni vzklikal, kajti voda je bila še vedno rjava in standard še vedno številka na kombiju.

**Wren Odira**  
Še vedno pravim, da je deset let povodec.

**Illuminara**  
Tudi jaz. Kaj bi spremenila?

**Wren Odira**  
Vsak mesec objavite tri številke na pomolu, kjer jih lahko prebere vsaka barka. Zakup, ki ga lahko bere vse pristanišče, je težje odpovedati kot tistega v predalu.

**Illuminara**  
To je močnejše od klavzule, ki sem jo napisala. Predloži svetu.
Odalys je na pultu odprla knjigo. Ni prosila za dovoljenje in ni ponudila, da jo bo pokazala. S svinčnikom je zapisala eno vrstico.
*Nedelja, Reed 7. Prepeljano. Tam.*

**Illuminara**  
Smem videti stran?

**Odalys Ferreira**  
Ne. To ni vaša stran.

Illuminara se je nasmehnila, česar pred neznanci ni počela pogosto. Zunaj na vodi je oseka tekla mimo tržnice nekoliko čistejša kot na dan njenega prihoda, Wren, ki je imela prav prvo jutro in bo glede zakupa imela prav čez deset let, pa je stala na pomolu in barkam na glas brala številke.

translation_sl.critic_line: Plavajoča tržnica preživi upravičen sanitarni rok, ker Illuminara Wrenin ugovor sprejme kot boljši model, z zapečatenim preizkusom dokaže nedeljsko izlivanje ter okoli zasebne privezne knjige skupnosti zgradi preverljiv izid, ne da bi si jo prilastila.
